These were checked on 22 November 2026 in throwaway repositories with uncommitted work by a person in the same file:

| Harness | Source of the patch | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OMP 19.0.1 | The harness's own record of which lines each agent wrote: `commit.draft("self")`, then `diff()`. Nothing is committed. | Edits made with its edit and write tools, per agent and subagent. A person's lines and another agent's lines in the same file were left out. Files written by a shell command are listed for review and are not in the patch. |
| Claude Code 2.1.311 | The agent follows the skill: it copies a file aside before each edit and appends `diff -u` after it. | Edits the agent recorded. It depends on the agent following the instructions from its first edit. |
| Codex CLI 0.171.0 | The same instructions. | The same. In its default sandbox Codex cannot reach Rex, so `--float` fails with `Rex did not open the review.` and the agent gives you the command to run. |

Claude Code and Codex can also run a program after each edit, which could record edits without relying on the agent. Milo does not install or ship such a program: it would change your agent's configuration, and what those programs receive for an edit differs by harness and version.

## Editing files

The reader only reads until you ask it to edit. Press `e`, or open the file with `milo view FILE --edit`, and the file's text becomes a draft with a cursor. It works the same in the reader Outline opens in its own pane, in the floating reader in Rex and in `milo view`. The last row lists the main keys, `Ctrl-G` opens help, and [keys and marks](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/keys.md#editing-in-the-reader) has the whole list.

The draft is yours alone until you save: the file on disk is not touched by typing, pasting, undoing or formatting. While you edit, the reader shows the draft with its code colours and no change marks. When you stop, it shows the file again at the same lines, with a fresh diff, and Outline still has the file selected.

If another program edits the file before you save, choose `c` at **Changed on disk** to compare the disk version (`−`) with your unsaved draft (`+`). Comparing does not write or merge anything. Press `Esc` to return to the choice, then `Esc` again to continue editing. [See the save conflict and comparison.](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/pane-compare-comparison.webp)

The editor is for small changes. It has one cursor and no selection or search, and it edits a file that exists: it does not make a new one. The cursor moves one character at a time, so an accent written as a separate mark takes a key press of its own.

### What can be edited

A working file can be edited when it is a regular file, is reached without passing through a link, holds UTF-8 text with no NUL bytes, is no larger than 2 MiB and can be written by you. A byte-order mark is allowed. Anything else stays read-only. The last row then never has `e edit`, and `e` or help says why. A narrow pane can also lack room for `e edit` on a file that can be edited; `e` works all the same.

| It says | Because |
| --- | --- |
| `this is a commit` | The reader shows the file as of a commit, from History or `--commit` |
| `this is a link` | The file is a link; the reader shows where it points |
| `reached through a link` | A folder on the way to the file is a link |
| `the project moved` | The project's folder was renamed or replaced after the reader opened |
| `outside the project` | The path leads out of the project |
| `the file is gone` | The file was removed; the reader may still show its removed lines |
| `not a regular file` | It is a folder, a device or a pipe |
| `not text` | It holds NUL bytes or is not UTF-8, which a save could not keep, or Git treats it as binary |
| `shown as a picture` | The reader is showing it as a picture |
| `it cannot be shown` | The reader shows a note in its place, such as `Too large to show.` |
| `too large` | It is larger than 2 MiB, though the reader can show its changes |
| `no write permission` | You may read it but not write it |
| `it cannot be read` | The file or a folder on the way could not be opened |

A draft cannot grow past 2 MiB either: a key or paste that would take it there is refused.

### Saving

`Ctrl-S` writes the draft into the file that was read. Milo does not put a new file in its place, so the file keeps its permissions, owner, other names and attributes. The bytes you did not edit stay the same: a byte-order mark is kept, every line keeps its own ending when a file mixes `LF` and `CRLF`, and a file with no final line break is not given one. A new line takes the ending most of the file uses.

Before it writes, milo opens the file again and reads it. Nothing is overwritten unexpectedly:

- If the file no longer holds what your edit started from, or another file has been put in its place, nothing is written. **Changed on disk** lets you compare, explicitly overwrite, or return to editing. If the file changes again before you confirm, Milo asks again.
- If the file is gone, it is not made again.
- If the file has become a link, or a folder on the way has become a link or moved, the save is refused. Milo never writes through a link.
- If you no longer have permission to write, the save is refused.

In each case the draft stays open, and the last row says what happened. If the write itself fails part of the way, milo puts the old contents back where it can and says whether it could.

A save writes in place, not through a temporary file; that is what keeps the file's links and attributes. A crash or power loss in the middle of a save can therefore leave a partly written file.

### Leaving unsaved changes

`Esc`, `Ctrl-Q` and `Ctrl-C` stop editing. With unsaved changes they ask `Unsaved edits: s save · d discard · Esc back` first. `q` is a letter while you edit. If the terminal has stopped taking output, `Ctrl-C` ends the reader at once, as it always has; the draft is then kept as described next.

Closing a [tab](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#tabs-in-the-floating-reader) that is being edited asks the same question, and the tab closes once you save or discard. `Ctrl-C` in a tab that is only being read would end the whole reader, so while another tab has unsaved changes it shows that tab and asks there instead. [See the question on closing a tab.](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/reader-tabs-close.webp)

A reader can also be ended from outside: its terminal is closed, the process is asked to stop, or Rex closes its pane. If it has unsaved changes, milo writes the draft to the `drafts` folder of its state folder (`~/.local/state/milo`, or `milo` under an absolute `$XDG_STATE_HOME`), readable only by you, and prints one line about it once the terminal is yours again: one draft and one line for each tab that had unsaved changes. The project is not written to. If milo has no state folder, because neither that variable nor `HOME` names one, the line says the edits were lost.

The next time you edit that file, the pane asks `Kept draft found: r restore · d delete · Esc later`. Restoring puts the kept text in place of the file's as one change, so `Ctrl-Z` shows the file as it is now. The kept copy is removed when you delete it or save the restored text, not before. If you defer or undo the restore and then the reader is closed from outside with new edits, both drafts are kept. After saving or deleting the offered draft, stop and start editing to see the next one. A process that is killed outright, or a machine that loses power, keeps nothing.

A kept draft remembers which text of the file it was written over. If the file holds something else by the time you restore it, because you, an agent or Git changed it meanwhile, the pane says `Draft restored over a changed file`, and the first `Ctrl-S` asks **Changed on disk** instead of writing, so you can compare the draft with what the file holds now before choosing. A draft kept by an earlier release of milo does not say what it was written over, so its first save asks too. [See the notice and the question, beside the save an earlier release made.](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/reader-draft-comparison.webp)

In Rex, a file from another project is never a tab: when the pane has followed the shell to another project, or its reader is gone, the next file opens a new floating reader in place of the old one. While the old one has unsaved changes in any tab, the pane says `The open reader has unsaved edits.` and leaves it alone.

## Formatting

While editing, `Ctrl-F` gives the draft to a formatter and puts its answer in place of the draft as one change. The file is not touched: look the result over, press `Ctrl-Z` to take it back, or discard it with the draft. Only `Ctrl-S` writes it. Keys pressed after `Ctrl-F` wait for the formatter and act on what it answered. If the formatter fails, the draft is left exactly as it was and the last row shows the first line of what the formatter said.

Milo runs a formatter you have installed. It does not install one, download one or run one through a package runner. For each kind of file, the first of these found is used:

| Files | Formatter | Run as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.rs` | rustfmt | `rustfmt --edition E --emit stdout` |
| `.go` | gofmt | `gofmt` |
| `.py`, `.pyi` | ruff, then black | `ruff format --no-cache --stdin-filename ./NAME -`<br>`black --quiet --stdin-filename ./NAME -` |
| `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.jsx`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.tsx`, `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.css` | prettier, then biome, then deno | `prettier --stdin-filepath ./NAME`<br>`biome format --stdin-file-path ./NAME`<br>`deno fmt --ext EXT -` |
| `.scss`, `.less`, `.html`, `.md`, `.yaml`, `.yml` | prettier, then deno | As above |
| `.vue` | prettier | As above |
| `.toml` | taplo | `taplo format --stdin-filepath ./NAME -` |
| `.c`, `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.hpp`, `.hh` | clang-format | `clang-format --assume-filename=NAME` |
| `.sh`, `.bash` | shfmt | `shfmt --filename ./NAME` |
| `.lua` | stylua | `stylua --stdin-filepath ./NAME -` |
| `.swift` | swift-format | `swift-format format --assume-filename ./NAME` |
| `.tf`, `.tfvars` | terraform | `terraform fmt -no-color -` |

`NAME` is the file's name and `EXT` its extension. For Rust, `E` is the edition in the nearest `Cargo.toml` at or above the file within the project, or 2021; the option is left out when a `rustfmt.toml` there sets an edition. Other kinds of file, including some the reader colours such as Kotlin, Ruby, Java, C#, PHP and SQL, have no formatter: `Ctrl-F` says `No formatter for this kind of file.` and the last row does not offer it.

How a formatter is run:

- **Only when you press `Ctrl-F`.** Opening, reading and editing a file never start one. Help looks for the program so that it can name it, and does not run it.
- **By name, from where you installed it.** The program is looked for in the folders of `PATH` that are written in full. A folder written relative to where milo runs, such as `.` or `node_modules/.bin`, is skipped, so a project cannot supply the program. The formatter's own `PATH` has those folders taken out too, so a launcher that starts `node` cannot find one in the project. If none is installed, the last row says which to install, for example `Not installed: ruff or black.`
- **On the draft, not the file.** The draft goes in on standard input and the formatted text comes back on standard output. The formatter is not asked to write anything.
- **In the file's folder, with the file's name.** That is how a formatter finds the project's settings, such as `rustfmt.toml`, `pyproject.toml` or `.prettierrc`. Those settings belong to the project, and some formatters load code named in them: Prettier loads plugins and JavaScript settings files. Format files only in a project you trust, as you would in an editor.
- **For at most ten seconds.** After that the formatter and the programs it started are stopped. A formatter that leaves a helper running with its output still open is waited for just as long, and its answer is not used. An answer that is empty, is not UTF-8 text or is larger than 2 MiB is refused.
- **Without downloads.** Milo installs nothing. A `rustfmt` installed by rustup is told not to fetch the toolchain a project's `rust-toolchain.toml` names: if that toolchain is missing, the last row says so.
- **Keeping the file's line endings.** If the file uses `CRLF` and the formatter answers with `LF`, the draft gets `CRLF` back. A byte-order mark is not given to the formatter and is kept.

The pane shows `Formatting with NAME…` and does not redraw until the formatter is done.

## Reading pictures, video and Markdown

Open a working file from Outline with `Enter` or a double-click. The preview is the file's Reader tab, not a browser, dev server or external player. `milo view FILE` uses the same path. History, `--commit` and handed-over patches still show the source/diff or a binary-file note; they never substitute today's file for the requested revision.

| Working file | macOS | Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PNG | Kitty bitmap where available; terminal cells otherwise | Kitty bitmap only; PNG must fit the 1,600-pixel side limit without resizing |
| JPEG, static WebP | Same as PNG, using the system image decoder | No conversion |
| MP4 | FFmpeg and FFprobe 8.0+ with `fd:` and `scale=…:reset_sar=1`, installed together in `/opt/homebrew/bin` or `/usr/local/bin` | Same tool capabilities, installed together in `/usr/bin` |
| `.md`, `.markdown` | Rendered terminal text; `m` for source or diff, `e` to edit | Same |

Milo asks recognized graphics terminals whether they support Kitty images. It sends a bitmap only after a positive reply. For an unrecognized terminal that supports the protocol, try `MILO_GRAPHICS=kitty milo view FILE`; `MILO_GRAPHICS=off` disables the query. Neither setting enables passthrough in a detected tmux or screen session. With a decoded image but fewer than 256 colours, Milo uses monochrome cells instead. A shell name or a `TERM` value alone is not proof that an emulator displayed an image.

**Pictures.** The image keeps its proportions and fits between the filename and the key hints. Input is limited to 64 MiB. The macOS decoder checks the format and dimensions, caps source images at 40 million pixels and 16,384 pixels per side, and has a five-second deadline. The Kitty bitmap is at most 1,600 pixels per side and 16 MiB; the cell raster is at most 512 pixels per side. Text named like a picture can still be read as text. Active documents such as SVG and PDF aren't rasterized.

Single-image GIF, BMP without linked profiles, and single-page TIFF without nested image directories are also recognized on macOS. Animated GIF/WebP, multi-page TIFF, HEIC/HEIF, PSD, ICO/ICNS, SVG and PDF aren't passed to a general-purpose converter.

**Video.** Opens paused. `Space` plays or pauses; `←` / `→` seek five seconds in either direction. Leaving the tab or opening help pauses playback. The Reader never opens an audio device. It streams scaled frames (up to 320 × 240 at 12 fps) as colored terminal cells. Only standalone MP4 with a local H.264, HEVC or MPEG-4 Part 2 video track is accepted, up to 128 MiB and one hour. The track header must fit 8,192 pixels per side; decoding is limited to 9.5 million pixels per frame. External tracks aren't followed. Milo looks for an already-installed decoder, never installs one, and gives a reason when it can't play a file.

Leaving an image or movie tab releases its prepared pixels and private movie snapshot. Returning loads the selected working file again. An unchanged movie remembers its paused position; a replaced movie starts from the beginning.

Media file reads run in the background. A canceled read still waiting on the filesystem keeps one of two slots until it returns; the Reader can still switch tabs or close. On macOS, a cloud placeholder must already be downloaded to open as media. Closing the Reader doesn't wait for cloud storage or start a download.

Limits on bytes, pixels and output apply before or during decoding. The macOS helper watchdog also stops a decoder observed above 384 MiB resident memory; this is sampled, not a hard ceiling on instantaneous process memory.

**Markdown.** Headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, emphasis and code render in the pane's own text styles. Links show text; embedded images show their labels, not fetched pixels. No HTML, scripts, URLs or file references are executed or loaded. `m` switches back and forth without losing the source diff. `e` opens the ordinary source editor; only an explicit save writes. Large previews stop at a labeled limit (512 KiB of text, 20,000 source lines or 32,000 wrapped rows); the source Reader keeps its own limits.

When another program saves or replaces the working file, the preview refreshes in place. An exclamation mark (`!`) identifies new or edited blocks for three seconds. These marks compare the last two previews, not the file against Git. If text moves above you, Milo keeps the passage you're reading in view when it can. Press `G` to follow the end instead. Scrolling (including the wheel), switching to source, or entering the editor stops following. `End` jumps to the bottom without following. A save on disk never replaces an open draft.

### Representative open times

Median of five release-build starts on an Apple M5 Pro, macOS 27.2.1, FFmpeg 9.0.2. Measured from spawning Milo to the first complete content frame on a 160 × 50 cell terminal. RSS is Milo's resident memory at that frame, not peak memory or the decoder's RSS. Release builds, terminal sizes and decoder builds affect these numbers.

| Fixture | Input bytes | First frame (ms) | Milo RSS (KiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1920 × 1080 PNG | 215,387 | 142.0 | 9,056 |
| 1920 × 1080 JPEG | 75,347 | 143.7 | 9,056 |
| 1920 × 1080 WebP | 46,604 | 140.3 | 8,992 |
| 1920 × 1080 H.264 MP4, 8 seconds | 5,557,338 | 141.2 | 7,920 |
| Markdown, 2,048 list items | 114,703 | 24.1 | 8,976 |

Reproduce with `python3 tests/rich_reader_bench.py target/release/milo`. Fixture generation uses local `ffmpeg` and `cwebp`; the reader doesn't need `cwebp`.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/keys.md

# Keys and marks

Press `?` for help when the pane has room. `Esc`, `q` or `?` closes help; `Ctrl-C` quits milo. Text pasted through a terminal that marks pastes is not read as key presses. While you are [editing a file](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/keys.md#editing-in-the-reader), the keys you type are text: help is `Ctrl-G`, and `Ctrl-C` asks before it gives up unsaved changes.

A help page longer than the pane continues in a second column, and a third, once the pane is 57 columns wide or more, so a full-width pane usually shows it whole. In the shell, `milo COMMAND --help` or `milo --help COMMAND` explains one command in a few lines, and `milo --help` lists every command and key.

In standalone Home, use `↑`/`↓` and `Enter` to choose a pane; the mouse is optional. `q` in a reader opened from Outline or History returns to the list, then `q` returns to Home. A pane started directly returns to the shell instead.

Pasting is distinct from typing only when the terminal supports bracketed paste and forwards its markers. Without it, pasted characters can act as shortcuts. Use the keyboard if your terminal or multiplexer intercepts mouse reports.

If your terminal sends an unfinished reply, or an Alt key produces the same prefix as a reply, Milo drops the ambiguous input rather than typing it. Press `Ctrl-X` to end that sequence. Then carry on typing, or press `Ctrl-C` to quit.

## Moving around

These keys work in the outline tree, history and reader. The reader and help page scroll instead of moving a selection.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Up / Down or `k` / `j` | Move one row |
| Page Up / Page Down or `Ctrl-B` / `Ctrl-F` | Move one page |
| `Ctrl-U` / `Ctrl-D` | Move half a page |
| Home / End or `g` / `G` | Go to the first or last row |
| Mouse wheel | Scroll |

### Outline

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | Open or close a folder, or read a file |
| `a` or `Ctrl-A` | Show Actions for the selected path in the tree |
| `Ctrl-T` or `Ctrl-A` in Find | Show Actions for the highlighted result. Typing `a` adds it to the query. |
| `Ctrl-O` / `Ctrl-R` | Open the selected working file in its default Mac app / reveal it in Finder; also works on the highlighted Find result |
| `Space` | Open or close a folder |
| Left or `h` | Close an open folder, or go to the parent |
| Right or `l` | Open a closed folder |
| `{` / `}` | Previous or next visible folder |
| `K` / `J` | Previous or next item in the same folder, skipping nested rows |
| `p` | Go to the parent folder |
| `e` | Open every folder; press again to restore your choices |
| `n` / `N` | Jump to the next or previous changed file, including inside closed folders. If there’s nowhere to jump, the tree says why. |
| `c` | Switch between the whole tree and changed files only |
| `/` | Find files by name or path; arrows choose a result, `Enter` reads it and `Esc` returns to the tree |
| `r` | Reload |
| `q` | Quit |

Click a folder to open or close it, click a file to select it, or double-click a file to read it. In the short Outline strip, double-click a filename to read it; a single click doesn’t scroll the strip. There’s no keyboard cursor: arrows, `h` / `l`, `j` / `k`, the wheel and Page Up / Page Down scroll one column at a time. Home / End or `g` / `G` go to either end.

### History

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Enter` | Show or hide a commit's files, show the rest of a long file list, or read the selected file |
| Left or `h` | From a file, return to its commit; from an open commit, close its file list |
| Right or `l` | Open the selected commit's files. In a narrow focused pane, page through a long subject first. |
| `r` | Reload |
| `q` | Quit |

Click a commit to toggle its files, click a file to select it, or double-click to read it as it was at that commit. For a merge, the file list compares the commit with its first parent.

### Reader

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `b` / `Space` | Scroll a page up or down |
| Left / Right or `h` / `l` | Scroll sideways |
| `m` in a working Markdown file | Switch between rendered text and the source/diff |
| `G` in rendered Markdown | Follow the end as the file changes. Any scroll stops following; `End` jumps once. |
| `Space` in a video | Play or pause (always muted) |
| Left / Right or `h` / `l` in a video | Seek back or forward five seconds |
| `n` / `N` | Next or previous block of added or removed lines |
| `c` | Switch between the full diff and changes with nearby context |
| `Tab`, then `Enter` | Select and expand a folded stretch of unchanged lines; clicking the fold expands it too |
| `e` | Edit the file, or say why it is read-only |
| `a` or `Ctrl-A` | Show Actions for the working file in read mode. When editing, `a` types a letter and `Ctrl-A` moves to the start of the line. |
| `Ctrl-O` / `Ctrl-R` | Open the shown working file in its default Mac app / reveal it in Finder (read mode only) |
| `q` or `Esc` | Close |

The last row shows `e edit` when the file can be edited and the row has room. Help lists the reason when it cannot, and the formatter that would run.

A [review of an agent's patch](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#reviewing-an-agents-edits), opened by `milo review PATCH`, adds `]` and `[` for the next or previous file of the patch and `r` to read the files again. It is always read-only.

### Editing in the reader

Press `e` in the reader, or start with `milo view FILE --edit`. The heading says `editing`, then `unsaved` once the draft differs from the file. Nothing is written until you save. See [editing files](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#editing-files) for what can be edited and how a save is kept safe.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl-S` | Save the draft to the file |
| `Ctrl-Z` / `Ctrl-Y` | Undo or redo. A run of typing is undone a word at a time |
| `Ctrl-F` | Format the draft with an [installed formatter](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#formatting). `Ctrl-Z` takes it back |
| `Esc`, `Ctrl-Q` or `Ctrl-C` | Stop editing. With unsaved changes, asks: `s` save, `d` discard, `Esc` back |
| Arrows | Move the cursor. Up and Down keep their column through shorter lines |
| Home / End or `Ctrl-A` / `Ctrl-E` | Start or end of the line |
| Page Up / Page Down | Move a page |
| `Enter` | New line, indented like the one above |
| `Tab` | Indent by a tab or by the file's own number of spaces |
| Backspace or `Ctrl-H` | Delete the character before the cursor |
| Delete or `Ctrl-D` | Delete the character under the cursor |
| `Ctrl-G` | Help |
| Click | Put the cursor there |
| Mouse wheel | Scroll without moving the cursor |

Pasted text is inserted as one change, with the file's line endings and without control characters. A paste larger than 1 MiB is refused. Every other key types itself, including `?` and `q`.

Once the floating reader in Rex holds a second file, `Ctrl-N` and `Ctrl-P` show the next and previous [tab](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#tabs-in-the-floating-reader) and `Ctrl-W` closes the shown one, while reading and while editing. A click on a tab's name shows it, and a click on its `×` closes it.

Questions take the place of the last row and wait for one of the keys they list. Any other key is ignored. When the pane is two rows tall they take the heading's row instead. A narrow pane drops the words before the keys first: at 28 columns every key is still listed.

| Question | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| `Unsaved edits` | `s` save and stop editing, `d` discard the draft, `Esc` go back to it |
| `Changed on disk` | `c` compare disk and draft, `o` overwrite the confirmed version, `Esc` back without writing |
| `Kept draft found` | `r` put the kept draft in place of the text, `d` delete it, `Esc` decide later |

### Usage and setup

In Usage, `r` checks local data without bypassing the [oh-my-pi read interval](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#where-the-figures-come-from), and `q` quits. In setup, use `1`–`4` or `Tab` for Layout, Appearance, Workflow and Health. Up / Down or `k` / `j` selects a row; `Enter` or `Space` activates it. In Layout, `a` tries the current draft and `u` undoes the trial. `s` asks **where** to save; choose the scope and confirm. `Esc` backs out of a confirmation without saving.

## Colours and marks

Milo uses the palette advertised by the terminal. Set `NO_COLOR=1` to suppress text colours without losing the selection indicator. Standalone panes default to plain file symbols; saved icon choices and `MILO_ICONS=plain`, `nerd` or `off` override the default. Rex keeps its Nerd Font default.

In a Git outline, **bold** means changes to commit and regular coloured names mean changes to push. Plain names have no changes marked.

If color or font weight is hard to distinguish, enable text change marks in setup. For a still outline while tools write files, choose static activity marks. Neither option changes the terminal's appearance for other programs.

| Colour | Change |
| --- | --- |
| Yellow | Edited |
| Green | Added; italic if Git does not track it yet |
| Red, struck through | Removed |
| Cyan, italic | Moved |
| Magenta | Left in conflict by a merge |

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Pulsing `●` / `○` at the left edge | Being written now |
| `•` at the left edge | Changed since you last looked |
| `docs 3` on a closed folder | Three changed files inside |
| `+7 −5` | Seven lines added and five removed |
| `○5 ↑2` in a narrow outline | Five files to commit and two to push |

When focus is elsewhere, the outline can follow the file being written (for example, `following tides.ts`). It does not move the cursor while you use it or reopen a folder you closed.

Following file activity and following a shell are different choices. File activity moves the outline selection within a project; shell following changes the project shown by an attached pane. Pin a pane's project if you want to keep reading it while the shell moves elsewhere.

In history, a hollow dot means uncommitted work. With a remote branch to compare against, a bold dot marks a commit not on that branch, and a faint dot marks one already on it. A regular dot means there is no comparison. The heading says `no branch tracked` if the current branch does not track a remote branch; that does not mean there are no commits to push. A `•` beside a commit means it arrived while the pane was open. Open a commit to see what changed in each file, in the same colours as the outline.

In the reader, added lines have a green background and keep their code colours; removed lines stay in place with a red background. If only some words of a line changed, those words are highlighted.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md

# Usage limits

`milo usage` shows how much of a reported limit is **left**, not how much has been used. It shows the tools that have something to show, and gives the whole pane to them. The two-row rail gives each of two tools one line for its most constrained window, and a tool on its own both rows. When there's room, it adds the reset countdown for a recent reading or when an older reading was last seen. Wide panes can show large figures and provider marks. Choose large figures in setup if you prefer them in a taller rail too.

A fresh **0% left** means the tool actually reported no remaining capacity. An older reading is marked as historical; once its reset time passes, Milo shows **reset elapsed**, not a fresh percentage. A missing reading is neither zero nor 100%. Run `milo doctor` to see which local source supplied a reading.

## macOS menu bar

With a menu-enabled CLI on macOS 13 or later, run `milo menubar install` to install and open `~/Applications/Milo.app`. Run it again to reopen or upgrade. `milo menubar uninstall` stops the app, unregisters launch at login if enabled, and removes only the app. Neither command needs sudo or a download.

If you have the older `Milo Usage.app`, run the install command again. It migrates the app to `Milo.app`; you don’t need to uninstall first.

You can also manage the menu app from Home (`milo`), under **Workflow** in terminal Settings (`milo setup`), or in the **Menu Bar** tab in web Settings (`milo web`). **Open or update** reopens the installed app or applies the CLI’s bundled update. Removal is a separate, confirmed action. It keeps the Milo CLI, your settings, and any unsaved Settings draft.

The Apple Silicon Homebrew and release binaries include the app. If you prefer to build it from source:

```sh
sh macos/build-menu.sh
./target/local-menu/milo menubar install
```

For a source build, use `./target/local-menu/milo` for subsequent menu commands. Both packaged and local builds omit personal paths. Run `milo menubar install` from the shell whose provider and configuration paths you want the menu to use; run it again if they change. These paths live in a private file beside the installed app, not in the signed bundle. The app has its own reader and does not require Rex.

If the CLI that installed the app has changed or moved, **Browser settings…** opens the bundled editor instead. Run `milo menubar install` from the new CLI to restore menu management from that editor.

Click the menu bar item to see the same local usage windows as the pane. The menu uses **global** provider visibility, not the preferences of whichever worktree happens to be focused. Automatic display picks the lowest fresh remaining percentage; when none is fresh it shows just Milo. Options lets you pin a provider, show only the mascot, or opt into launch at login. Quitting the app also stops its reader.

Hover over the percentage to see which provider and limit it represents, how much is left, and when it resets if known. Open the menu to see that same window first. Icon-only mode keeps the usual provider order.

In **More options → Menu bar indicator**, choose **CPU** or **Memory** to put a system reading beside Milo instead. The same choice is in **Workflow → Menu bar indicator** in `milo setup` and the browser editor’s **Menu Bar** tab. From a shell, use `milo menubar indicator` followed by `quota`, `cpu`, or `memory`. The choice is saved for this Milo profile, not per project, and doesn’t install the app. In either system mode, click Milo to see both readings under **This Mac**, above your agent limits. Switch back to **Agent quota** (the default) to restore your previous quota display and stop system sampling.

- **CPU** is the percentage of time all logical cores together were busy over the last sample interval. All cores busy is 100%, not 100% per core. The first reading, including after wake, is a dash until Milo has two usable samples.
- **Memory** is physical RAM used, not memory pressure. The popover shows used / installed GiB. Using the names from `vm_stat`, used pages are **anonymous − purgeable + wired down + occupied by compressor**. This counts the compressor’s actual RAM once, excludes file cache and swap, and need not match Activity Monitor’s “Memory Used” exactly.

The running app reads macOS counters about every five seconds in system modes. Readings stay in memory: no history, network requests, permissions or extra service. A stalled sample or counter reset doesn’t turn into a zero or a spike.

Low-quota notifications are **off by default**. In **More options → Low-quota alerts**, choose 10%, 20%, or 30% remaining and allow notifications when macOS asks. Milo alerts only when a visible provider’s fresh reading moves from above your threshold to at or below it, at most once for that provider and reset time. Starting below the threshold is silent. Stale, elapsed, hidden, and unknown-reset readings do not trigger alerts. Choose **Off** to stop them.

![Milo’s native menu with example Codex and Claude limits and the Settings button](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/img/menu-bar.webp)

Choose **Browser settings…** to open the [local browser editor](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#browser-editor). To change a specific worktree instead, run `milo web` from that project.

## Which tools appear

Milo gives a tool a place once it has a figure, and no place before that. If you use Codex and Claude Code but not OpenCode, the pane has two places and nothing for OpenCode: no label, no dash and no empty row. Each tool has its own choice under **Appearance** in `milo setup` or **Usage** in `milo web`, saved globally or for a worktree like the other pane preferences. Reopen the pane to apply a change.

| Choice | What the pane does |
| --- | --- |
| Auto, the default | Gives the tool a place while it has a figure saved on this Mac: a limit window for Codex or Claude Code, or tokens OpenCode recorded today. Without one the tool takes no room. |
| Always show | Keeps the tool's place even without a reading. Milo says what it knows, such as `no sessions found` or `could not read saved limits`, instead of inventing a percentage. A pane too small for every tool gives its rows to limits first. |
| Hide | Never shows the tool and does not look for it: its folders are not walked or watched, and its database is not opened. With Codex and Claude Code both hidden, oh-my-pi's database is not opened either. |

Whether a tool is in use here is read from files the tool itself saved. Milo does not run the tool, read its sign-in or use the network to find out.

| Tool | Found when |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | A session file `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` has something in it, or oh-my-pi has saved a Codex report. |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude.json` has something in it, or a session written today is under `~/.claude/projects`, or the status line or oh-my-pi has saved a limit report. |
| OpenCode | The file where it keeps its database is a SQLite database. |

Empty folders, empty files, another kind of file under the same name and a Claude Code directory that holds only settings do not count. Links to individual sources or within the session trees are not followed. A report oh-my-pi saved for a tool does count, even when nothing else of the tool is on disk. The looks are the bounded reads described under [Where the figures come from](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#where-the-figures-come-from).

Milo uses `$CODEX_HOME/sessions` instead of `~/.codex/sessions` when Codex has an explicit home. With `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set, it looks for `.claude.json`, `projects/` and `settings.json` inside that directory, not in the default profile. Run Milo and Claude Code with the same override to see and configure that profile's usage.

A tool that is found but has no figure yet stays out of the way of the tools that have one. When no tool has a figure, the pane shows one quiet block instead of empty places: what each found tool is waiting for, such as `Claude · no saved limits found` and `Run milo setup`, or `No usage to show yet` and the tools Milo looks for when it found none.

The frame closes up around what is shown:

- **Two tools with limits** share the pane: side by side when it is wide, one above the other on a rail.
- **One tool with limits** has the pane to itself. A rail lists its other windows under the tightest one, and a wide pane keeps its windows together at the left.
- **OpenCode with one of them** takes the second place: the other half of a wide pane, or the lower half of a rail.
- **OpenCode with both** has one row beneath them, from the third row of a rail or in a wide pane at least nine rows tall. Two rows go to the two limits.
- **OpenCode alone** fills the two-row rail with today's tokens, then its cost and steps. A larger pane draws the tokens large.

`milo doctor` follows the same rule. It reports a tool that was found or is always shown, and says nothing of one that is absent or hidden beyond the choice itself.

## Where the figures come from

| Source | What milo reads |
| --- | --- |
| oh-my-pi | Limits the harness saves for Codex and Claude in `~/.omp/agent/agent.db` (or `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/agent.db`). Milo reads only the usage data, using `/usr/bin/sqlite3` in read-only mode. Automatic reads are at least 20 seconds apart per pane. |
| Codex | Limit reports in recent Codex session files under `~/.codex/sessions` |
| Claude Code | Its own saved limits in `~/.claude.json`, or limits sent through the status line if you turn it on in setup. |
| OpenCode | Today's activity, not limits, from its session database. See [OpenCode activity](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#opencode-activity). |

For each tool, milo uses the newest report it can read. When there is room, it also shows **tokens today** from Claude Code's local session files under `~/.claude/projects`. This is local activity since midnight, not a limit. It counts new input, output and cache writes, not cache reads. A `+` after the number means the total may be incomplete.

If a clock or time-zone change moves the start of today earlier, Milo checks unchanged transcripts again for the newly included activity.

A report dated more than five minutes ahead of this machine's clock is not used, whichever source it came from. Otherwise one report written while a clock was wrong would outrank every later one. Milo shows the newest of the remaining sources instead. A deferred Codex or Claude Code report becomes eligible as the clock catches up, even if the source file has not changed. For the status-line save, the next report from Claude Code replaces the misdated file.

Milo checks the tails of recent Codex logs, then resumes near the previous end as those logs grow. Ordinary session activity does not clear the last limit report. A new or replaced log, a truncation, or a large burst of new data calls for another bounded tail check.

While a Codex log has been active in the last five minutes, Milo checks known logs about every two seconds, even if the writer keeps the file open. With a native watcher, Milo groups notifications so it doesn’t walk the session directories on every write. Without a watcher, it looks for new Codex and Claude Code sessions on the roughly two-second fallback checks. Press `r` to check immediately.

Milo labels reports as older after five minutes, or ten minutes for oh-my-pi to allow for its provider refresh cadence. This uses the time the provider's window was last observed, not the time Milo read the file.

**Show Claude Code limits** in `milo setup` adds a status line if you do not already have one. Claude Code calls `milo claude-status` to show a short line and save the reported limits to `~/.local/state/milo/claude-limits.json` (or under an absolute `$XDG_STATE_HOME`). It does not save prompts or replies. You do not need to enable it if Claude Code or oh-my-pi already saves a report.
Each explicit `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` has its own `claude-limits.json` under Milo's `claude-profiles/` state directory, so a reading from another profile is not used as a fallback.
Within a profile, Milo uses Claude Code's saved account ID to keep limits tied to the signed-in account. Switching accounts hides the old limits; the next status report starts with only the windows it supplies. Milo does not read the sign-in token.

An unchanged status-line reading confirms the same window, but Milo saves that confirmation at most once a minute per window. A lower figure for the same window or an older reset does not replace or refresh the saved figure.
If an update leaves out the reset time, it can update a nondecreasing figure without discarding the last known reset.

## OpenCode activity

OpenCode saves no limits on this machine, so Milo shows none for it. What it does save is each step's token counts and its own cost estimate. Beneath two tools with limits Milo gives it one line, such as `OpenCode · 48.2k tokens today · $1.37 est.`. A narrower pane drops the cost first, then shortens the rest. Beside one tool, or alone, it also shows the number of steps, when the last one was recorded and the cache reads. [Which tools appear](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#which-tools-appear) says where it goes at each size.

| Figure | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Tokens today | New input, output, reasoning and cache writes of the assistant steps OpenCode recorded since local midnight, in every project. Cache reads are left out, as they are for Claude Code. It is activity, not a share of any limit. |
| Cost | The sum OpenCode recorded for those steps, in US dollars. It is OpenCode's estimate from model prices, not a bill: a subscription or an unpriced model records zero, and Milo shows nothing rather than `$0`. A `+` means some steps recorded no cost. |
| Limits | Unknown. OpenCode asks its own servers for allowances and budgets when you open them, and does not save the answer. Milo does not ask and does not use OpenCode's saved sign-in. |

Milo reads `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, or the same file under an absolute `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, or the file `$OPENCODE_DB` names. It uses `/usr/bin/sqlite3` in read-only mode for at most a second, at least 20 seconds apart, and reads a database nothing has written to since the last read again only every five minutes. The queries return sums and times only: message text never leaves the database, and the tables that hold OpenCode's sign-in are not read. The line can lag OpenCode by about half a minute; press `r` to read now.

The figures were checked against databases written by OpenCode 1.2.0, 1.19.6, 2.2.0 and 2.3.2. They match `opencode stats --days 0`, except that Milo does not count a forked session's copied steps again on the day OpenCode 1 is upgraded to 2. Milo shows nothing, and `milo doctor` reports OpenCode's activity as unknown, when the database has other tables, when a step from today is malformed, when one of today's sessions was created by a version other than 1.x or 2.x, or when OpenCode 1 is still writing to a database OpenCode 2 has upgraded. Title requests are not counted, nor are OpenCode 2's compaction requests, because OpenCode does not record them as steps. [Usage sources](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage-sources.md) has the evidence, the limits of this reading, and why Amp and Gemini CLI are not read.

## Accounts asked online

Some figures exist only on a provider's servers. Milo can ask for four of them, and asks for none until you turn that account on. Each is hidden by default: with the choice left at **Hide**, Milo does not read the key, does not contact the provider and shows nothing, whatever keys are in your environment.

| Account | What the provider reports | What it is not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek | The prepaid API **balance**, in yuan or dollars, and the part of it that was granted | A limit, or what you spent |
| OpenRouter | What is **left of the key's spending limit** in dollars, or what the key has used when it has no limit; and its spend today and this month | Your account's credit balance, which needs a management key Milo does not ask for |
| Devin | **ACUs** your organization consumed in Devin's current billing day, which starts at 08:00 UTC | What is left of a plan. Enterprise plans only |
| Copilot | GitHub **AI credits** your personal account consumed this calendar month | What is left of the monthly allowance, which the API does not report. Not for seats billed to an organization |

These are money and counts, so they are written out in words, such as `DeepSeek · ¥110.00 balance` or `Devin · 12.5 ACUs today`. They are never drawn as a percentage or a large figure, never pick the menu bar badge and never raise a low-quota alert. An answer older than two refreshes is marked with its age; one older than a day, or from a billing day or month that has ended, is dropped.

**Turn an account on** under **Usage** in `milo web`, or in `~/.config/milo/preferences.conf` (a worktree can have its own choice, like the tools):

```
usage_deepseek = auto
usage_openrouter = always
usage_devin = hide
usage_copilot = hide
```

**Auto** asks the provider and gives the account a place once it has a figure. **Always show** also keeps the place to say why there is none, such as `no key set`, `key was refused` or `rate limited`. Terminal Settings (`milo setup`) does not list accounts yet.

**Give Milo a key of its own.** Milo reads only these names, from the environment of the shell that starts the pane, or from `~/.config/milo/usage-accounts.conf`:

| Account | Settings | The key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DeepSeek | `MILO_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | An API key from the DeepSeek platform |
| OpenRouter | `MILO_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | An ordinary API key; one with its own spending limit shows what is left of it |
| Devin | `MILO_DEVIN_API_KEY`, `MILO_DEVIN_ORG` (`org-…`) | A service user key or personal access token with the `ViewOrgConsumption` permission |
| Copilot | `MILO_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `MILO_GITHUB_USER` | A fine-grained personal access token with read access to the account's **Plan** |

```
# ~/.config/milo/usage-accounts.conf — chmod 600
MILO_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY = sk-…
```

The file must be a plain file of yours that no one else can read, or Milo ignores it and says so. The environment wins over the file. The macOS menu bar app does not inherit your shell's environment, so it needs the file. Milo does not look at `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `GH_TOKEN` or any key another tool keeps: a key reaches a provider only because you named it for Milo. Prefer a key made for this, with the least access the provider offers. A DeepSeek key can also spend the balance, so treat the file like the key itself.

**What is sent and kept.** One `GET` over HTTPS to the provider's own host, through `/usr/bin/curl`, with the key passed on curl's standard input rather than its command line. Redirects are not followed. Milo normally asks DeepSeek and OpenRouter every 5 minutes, Devin and Copilot every 15, and asks again when the billing day or month their count covers ends. If a provider cannot be reached, Milo can retry after one minute instead of waiting the full interval. `r` asks again, but no sooner than 30 seconds after the last request and never inside a rate limit the provider announced. A refused key is not offered again for 30 minutes unless you press `r`. The figures and times of the last answer are saved under `~/.local/state/milo/accounts/` so that panes and the menu using the same credentials can share an answer; the key is never written there.
Each provider, key and organization or user has its own saved answer and retry timing. Panes, the menu and `milo doctor` use only the entry for the credentials they read. Changing a key in the private settings file clears the old figure on the next check, even if its refresh was still pending.

While Milo is running, retry waits use elapsed time, so a wall-clock change does not shorten or extend them. Saved retry times still let a pane or menu opened later respect the last request.

**Where it appears.** Limits keep their rows first, then OpenCode, then accounts: one row each at the foot of the pane, or the whole pane when no tool has a place. The menu lists each account with its figure in words.

Using DeepSeek or OpenRouter through OpenCode shows two different things: OpenCode's estimate of what today's steps cost, and what the provider says is left. Milo shows each under its own name and does not combine them.

## What milo does not do

For the tools above, the usage pane reads local data. It does not call their providers, run the tools, sign in, read their saved credentials, guess limits from token counts or work out a cost from them. Figures can be old or missing if no tool has saved a report on this machine recently. The status-line helper writes its own limit readings, not the session logs.

The one exception is an [account you turn on](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#accounts-asked-online). For that account alone Milo sends one request to the provider's documented endpoint, with a key you set for Milo. It never turns a balance, a spend or a count of credits into a percentage, never adds figures from different accounts together, and never uses a key another tool saved.

## If a figure is missing

- A tool that is not there at all has no figure saved on this Mac, or is hidden. Run `milo doctor` to see what Milo found, or choose **Always show** for it in setup to keep its place and see what it is waiting for.
- Make the pane taller and wider to see labels, reset times and hints. Where the terminal can show pictures, including in Rex, milo draws the logos and large figures as pictures. Otherwise it draws with text. Short panes use text either way.
- Press `r` to check local data immediately. Milo reuses any oh-my-pi check already in progress and updates the pane when it finishes. Existing figures stay visible; `checking` means a lookup is in progress and there is no figure yet. For a tool, reload does not ask a provider for a fresh reading; for an account you turned on, it asks again at most every 30 seconds.
- A tool that is always shown, or found while no tool has a figure, says why it has none. `no sessions found` means no Codex sessions were found; `no limits to show` means there are sessions but no usable limits, or that a saved report has no windows. `no saved limits found` means milo has no saved Claude Code reading. `no tokens recorded today` means OpenCode's database has nothing from today. A narrow pane may shorten these hints.
- For oh-my-pi, check that `/usr/bin/sqlite3` is available and the harness has saved a report. For Claude Code, see [setup](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#claude-code-limits) if neither saved source has a reading.
- An account that is turned on but missing has no figure yet and is set to Auto. Run `milo doctor`: it names the setting each account reads, where it found the key, and what the last answer or failure was, without asking the provider again. Choose **Always show** to see the reason in the pane. On a two-row rail with two limits, raise **Usage height** to give an account a row.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md

# Discord presence

Milo can show on your Discord profile that you are using Rex. It is off until you turn it on, and while it is off Milo starts nothing for it and never contacts Discord.

## What becomes public

While presence is on and a Rex app has a session open on this computer, the Discord app shows this as your activity:

- **Milo's name and icon**, from Milo's public Discord application
- one fixed line under it: **In a Rex session**

Anyone who can see your Discord activity sees it, and so can tell when you are using Rex. Discord decides who that is and may add how long the activity has been up. Use Discord's own activity privacy settings to narrow it.

That is all, unless you choose to show more. There are four choices of **details**, and the first is the default:

| Details | Adds a second line | For example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `generic` | nothing | |
| `session` | the name of the Rex session in front | Session: release-notes |
| `project` | the folder name of the Git project in that session's focused pane | Project: milo |
| `both` | both names | Project: milo · Session: release-notes |

A session's name is whatever you or a coding agent called it, and often describes the work, so read it as others would before showing it. A project's name is the folder name of its Git repository: never its path, its remote address or a branch.

Whatever you choose, Milo never sends a tab title, a file name, a path, a remote address, a command, a terminal title or anything a terminal shows. Each name is cut to one short line of plain text. A name that could be a path or an address, one with a `/`, a `\` or a `user@host:` form, is left out whole.

Every place you can turn presence on, or choose to show a name, says what that makes public before it does. Turning presence on does not turn names on, and a choice saved by an earlier Milo keeps showing only what it showed then.

### Which session is “in front”

Names come only from the session the Rex app on this computer is showing: the one whose active tab has its focused pane held by that app. Rex has no call that names the session an app is looking at, so Milo goes by that. If two sessions fit, or none does, Milo shows no name at all rather than the name of the wrong session, and `milo presence` says so. This happens once the app has shown more than one session, or while only a phone or another computer is attached. Outside a Git project there is no project name.

With `generic`, Milo asks Rex one thing: whether any Rex app has a session open. It looks at no session. With a name chosen, it also asks which session is in front and, only for the names you chose, that session's label and the folder its focused pane is working in.

## Turn it on

Nothing needs creating first: Milo shows the activity under its own Discord application. An application ID is public, not a password. Milo holds no bot, token or client secret, and never signs in to Discord.

Use any one of these:

- `milo presence enable`. It says what becomes public and asks before turning anything on. `--yes` answers for you in a script.
- `milo setup`, then **Workflow → Discord presence**.
- `milo web`, then **Integrations → Discord presence → Turn on…**.

All three read and write the same saved choice, `discord.conf` in Milo's settings folder. It is one choice for your account on this computer, not a per-worktree preference, and it is saved at once without the **Save** step that pane preferences use.

To show a name, choose it in the same place: `milo presence details session`, `project`, `both` or back to `generic`; **Presence shows** in Settings; or **Shows** in the browser editor. While presence is on, a choice that adds a name asks first, and one that removes a name takes it down at once.

### Your own application

To show a name and icon of your choosing in place of Milo's:

1. Open <https://discord.com/developers/applications>, choose **New Application** and name it. The name is what Discord shows, as in “Playing Rex”. An app icon is optional. No bot is needed.
2. Copy the **Application ID** from its General Information page. It is a number of 17 to 19 digits.
3. Give it to Milo: `milo presence application APPLICATION_ID`, **Presence application** in Settings, or **Use your own Discord app** in the browser editor. A terminal's paste is not read in Settings, so the command is easier for a copied ID.

`milo presence application official`, or the same control in Settings and the browser editor, goes back to Milo's. An application ID you saved with an earlier Milo is kept until you do.

## Check it and turn it off

`milo presence` says whether presence is on, which application and details it uses, and what Discord is showing now, names included. The same line appears under **Discord presence** in Settings, in the browser editor and in `milo doctor`.

| It says | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Discord is showing “In a Rex session”. | The activity is up, with any names it lists. |
| …with no name: Milo has none it can be sure of. | Names are chosen, but [no one session is in front](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md#which-session-is-in-front) or it has no name to show. |
| Nothing is shown until a Rex app opens a session. | Rex is running, but no Rex app has a session open. |
| The Discord app is not running here. | Milo looks for it every 10 seconds while Rex is in use. |
| Discord does not know this application ID. | Check the ID, or go back to Milo's application. |
| Milo's presence helper is not running. | See [when it runs](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md#when-it-runs). |
| Discord did not accept the activity. | Discord answered with an error. Nothing is shown until presence is turned on again or Rex restarts. |

`milo presence disable`, or the same switch in Settings or the browser editor, takes the activity down at once, closes Milo's connection to Discord and stops the helper. Nothing then runs until you turn presence on again. Your choice of details and application is kept.

## When it runs

While presence is on, one small helper process does the work. Rex tells it when the first Rex app opens a session and when the last one leaves; it puts the activity up and takes it down to match. However many tabs, sessions and Milo panes are open, there is one helper and one connection to Discord, so nothing competes to set your activity.

With names chosen, Rex also tells the helper when a tab, a pane, a session's name or a pane's program changes. The helper waits a second for such changes to settle, and tells Discord only if the line it would show is different. Changing the details or the application replaces the helper: the old activity is taken down before the new one is put up.

The helper starts when you turn presence on while Rex is running, and whenever Rex loads Milo's saved layout, which is each time Rex starts once you have saved a layout in `milo setup` with at least one pane or with **Arrange new shell tabs** on. It ends when the Rex server stops. Without a saved layout, run `milo presence enable` again after starting Rex.

If Discord is not running, or quits, the helper waits and puts the activity back within about 10 seconds of Discord returning. Quitting Rex or turning presence off takes the activity down. So does **Uninstall Milo** in Home, which also turns presence off, so a later install starts with it off. If you remove the binary another way, run `milo presence disable` first. Rex itself is never slowed or changed by any of this: the helper only listens.

## Platforms and limits

- Presence talks to the **Discord desktop app** on the same computer and account as Milo, through the [local connection Discord documents](https://docs.discord.com/developers/topics/rpc). The browser and mobile versions of Discord have none, and nothing is shown through them alone.
- Milo's prebuilt release is for Apple Silicon Macs. A source build on Linux looks for Discord's socket in `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` as Discord documents; a Discord installed as a Flatpak or Snap keeps its socket elsewhere and is not found.
- Only a Rex app with a session open counts. Scripts, the `rex` command and Milo's own listener do not, and a Rex app left open counts for as long as it has a session open, whether or not you are at the keyboard.
- Presence follows the Rex server on this computer. Sessions on another host do not start it there, and names are never taken from them.
- Names are shown only [when one session is plainly in front](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md#which-session-is-in-front). Expect the fixed line alone after you have looked at several sessions.
- The fixed line's wording cannot be changed. To change the name or icon, use [an application of your own](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md#your-own-application).
- If Discord rejects an application ID, Milo stops asking until you turn presence on again or Rex restarts.

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/integrations.md

# Milo integrations

Milo works in a supported terminal without Rex or a connected account. Pick the integration for the job: reading local usage, checking an online account, forwarding an alert, or opening a file. These are separate choices.

## Coding agents and usage

`milo usage` reads reports already on disk. It doesn’t launch a harness or sign in to discover one. **Auto** keeps tools without a reading out of the way; **Hide** stops checking that tool. See [usage settings and local sources](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#which-tools-appear).

| Local source | What shows up in Milo |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | Limit windows recorded in recent sessions. |
| Claude Code | Saved limit windows and, when available, today’s transcript token count. An optional Claude Code status line can supply limit reports. |
| oh-my-pi (OMP) | Saved Codex and Claude limit reports contribute to those tools’ readings, not a separate OMP quota. |
| OpenCode | Today’s recorded tokens, steps and estimated cost from its local database. Not a remaining quota. |

**Agent patch review** is separate from usage detection: a harness that can hand over a recorded patch can use `milo review PATCH`. This shows that patch rather than treating every change in the worktree as the agent’s. See the [Milo agent skill](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/skills/milo/SKILL.md).

## Online provider accounts

These are **off by default**. Enable an account and supply its own credential to query the provider. Milo doesn’t reuse a harness login. Balances, spend and credits are not quota percentages.

| Provider | What the API reports |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek | Prepaid balance in the account currency. |
| OpenRouter | The key’s remaining spending limit or its spend; account credits require a management key. |
| GitHub Copilot | AI credits consumed this month, not credits remaining; access depends on the plan and token permissions. |
| Devin | Daily ACUs consumed for an eligible Enterprise organization, not an allowance remaining. |

See [account setup](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#accounts-asked-online) and the [provider evidence](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage-sources.md#summary), including access restrictions and schema-only checks. Cursor, Gemini CLI and Amp are not shipped usage adapters.

## Rex, messaging and the Mac menu bar

| Integration | What it adds | Where to start |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rex | Remembered pane layouts, floating Reader tabs, shell following and access to another host’s local settings dashboard. | [Setup and hosts](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md) |
| Discord alerts | Forward selected Rex events to a channel. Pair through Milo or use your own webhook. Delivery goes directly from your device to Discord. | [Alert forwarding](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#mirror-rex-alerts) |
| Telegram alerts | Pair with Milo’s bot in a private chat (delivery uses the hosted relay), or configure your own bot and chat without the relay. Can run alongside Discord. | [Alert forwarding](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/setup.md#mirror-rex-alerts) |
| Discord Rich Presence | Optionally show Rex activity in Discord. Separate from alerts; session and project names are separate opt-ins. | [Presence and privacy](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/presence.md) |
| Milo for macOS | Optional menu app for agent quota or local CPU/memory readings, with access to settings. Included in the Apple Silicon release; installed separately with `milo menubar install`. | [Menu bar guide](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/usage.md#macos-menu-bar) |

## Reader, media and file tools

- **Git** supplies worktree changes, commit history and historical file contents. Outline also browses plain folders. [Pane guide](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md)
- **Markdown** renders directly in Reader in the **v0.1.7 release**; no external previewer is required. On **main**, the [Actions menu](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#file-actions) also offers an explicit handoff to a user-installed **tkmp** beside the Rex shell for eligible working Markdown files. That handoff is not in v0.1.7. Milo passes the filename only; see the [wrapper for width-capable builds](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#using-the-full-pane-width-with-tkmp). A built-in fit-to-pane choice is tracked separately in [#94](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/issues/94) and depends on [tfcace/tkmp#1](https://github.com/tfcace/tkmp/pull/1).
- **Kitty graphics** can display supported images after a positive terminal capability check. **FFmpeg and FFprobe** are optional, user-installed tools for supported MP4s. The [format matrix](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#reading-pictures-video-and-markdown) lists platform fallbacks and decoder requirements.
- **Finder and default Mac apps** can reveal or open eligible working files on a verified local Mac. These actions don’t export a draft or open today’s file in place of a historical revision. [Native file actions](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#opening-a-file-outside-milo-on-a-mac)
- **Formatters** run on request against the draft: rustfmt, gofmt, Ruff, Black, Prettier, Biome, Deno, Taplo, clang-format, shfmt, StyLua, swift-format and Terraform. Milo doesn’t download them or save their output without your explicit save. [File types and formatter selection](https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/docs/panes.md#formatting)

---

Source: https://github.com/mcc0x/milo/blob/main/skills/milo/SKILL.md

name: milo
description: Use milo in a user's terminal to show a Git file tree, recent commits, usage, a file from the working tree or a commit, or only the edits you made yourself, and to guide Rex setup.
